extracted.intended_audience: IP office statisticians, policymakers, researchers, and analysts of trademark filing and registration trends
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, metrics and evaluation criteria used in WIPO's trademark statistics (application and registration counts, class counts, resident/non-resident measures, Nice classification and sector groupings, and adjustments for GDP/population). Intended to guide compilation and interpretation of international trademark data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application class count
rubrics_metrics.description: The total number of Nice classes specified in trademark applications received by offices; used to make international comparisons of filing activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many offices classify applications according to one or more of 45 Nice classes. Some offices allow only single-class filing while others permit multi-class filings; counting classes (rather than applications) improves comparability across offices. This method for comparing offices began in 2004, the first year for which complete class count data are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Nice Classification (45 classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international classification of goods and services used for registering trademarks and service marks; applications are classified into one or more of 45 Nice classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nice classification statistics provide insights into the relative importance of different goods and services. Top Nice classes (by non-resident filing) in 2023 included class 9, 35, 42, 5 and 25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-class versus multi-class filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an office permits only single-class filings (separate application per class) or allows multi-class filings (one application specifying multiple classes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differences in filing format affect raw application counts; class counts are preferred for international comparison because they account for multi-class filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident and non-resident application class counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Partitioning application class counts by applicant origin: resident (filed at national/regional office by local applicants) versus non-resident (filed by applicants based outside the office's jurisdiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute the non-resident share (%) of filing. Trends in resident vs non-resident filing can differ across years and offices and help explain growth/decline patterns (e.g., 84.2% resident share globally in 2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident share (proportion of filing from non-residents)
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of total application class counts at an office that originate from non-resident applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global non-resident share fell from 27.7% in 2009 to 15.8% in 2023, largely owing to high volumes of resident filing in certain countries (notably China). Offices with high non-resident shares (e.g., Canada, Switzerland, Australia, EUIPO, UK, US) indicate stronger foreign-filing attraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent application class count (regional multiplier)
rubrics_metrics.description: For regional IP offices, each application is multiplied by the number of member states for origin-based reporting (e.g., an EUIPO application by a non-EU applicant is counted as 27 applications abroad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This multiplier is applied to both applications and the classes specified therein; it is employed when reporting data based on an applicant's origin to reflect the effect of regional filing routes (and can materially inflate abroad counts due to the multiplier effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application class counts adjusted for GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident application class counts normalized per USD 100 billion of GDP to compare filing intensity relative to economic size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusting for GDP can change rankings (smaller-economy countries with fewer absolute classes may rank higher when normalized). Examples: China, Türkiye, Republic of Korea, Brazil and Russian Federation showed high ratios in 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application class counts adjusted for population
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident application class counts expressed per million population to measure filing intensity relative to population size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for comparing intensity across countries of different population sizes. Example: Republic of Korea had 5,120 resident application class counts per million in 2023; Switzerland and China also had high per-capita ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trend and year-on-year growth rates (applications and class counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual totals and growth rates for applications and application class counts over time (e.g., 2009–2023), expressed as absolute counts and percent growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trends capture long-term shifts and short-term fluctuations (e.g., 2021 spike in non-resident filing, steep declines in 2022 and 2023). Year-on-year comparisons should account for exceptional events and policy/behavioral shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of filing by Nice class and goods/services split
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of non-resident filing by individual Nice classes and by whether the class is goods or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 2023 goods class 9 accounted for 11.4% of non-resident filing by class; services classes (11 classes) represented 30.3% of all Nice classes specified in applications filed abroad. Office-level shares vary substantially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping Nice classes into industry sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregation of the 45 Nice classes into 10 industry sectors (e.g., research & technology, health, clothing and accessories) to analyze sectoral filing patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sector grouping reveals which industries attract the most foreign trademark protection; e.g., research & technology accounted for 20.1% of non-resident filing in 2023, followed by health (13.7%) and clothing (12.4%). Sector composition varies by office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration counts and registration class counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of trademarks registered (number of registrations) and the number of classes specified in registrations (registration class counts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrations can fluctuate year-to-year due to application volumes and offices' examination capacity; registration counts in a given year should not be directly compared to applications filed in the same year because of processing lags. In 2023 an estimated 7.6 million registrations and about 10.3 million registration classes were recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active trademark registrations in force
rubrics_metrics.description: The stock of registrations maintained (in force) across offices at a point in time, reflecting renewals and the longevity of marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active registrations can grow even when annual registrations decline due to renewals and past examination decisions. Example: estimated 88.2 million active registrations across 155 offices in 2023, a 6.4% increase over 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing abroad / origin-based filing behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of the volume and share of filing that applicants direct to foreign jurisdictions (filing abroad) and the origins supplying non-resident filing at particular offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis includes equivalent application class counts abroad by origin and the shares of non-resident filing at receiving offices (e.g., which origins supply most non-resident filing to China, US, EUIPO, etc.). Patterns reflect market attractiveness, geographic proximity and historical ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution of resident and non-resident filing to office growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Decomposition of an office's year-on-year growth in application class counts into components attributable to resident filing versus non-resident filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains drivers of growth/decline at office level (e.g., some offices saw resident increases offsetting non-resident decreases, others experienced declines driven mainly by resident filing reductions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office procedural and performance indicators (TOC-listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational metrics collected for offices such as distribution of examination outcomes, potentially pending applications, number of examiners, duration of examination, third-party oppositions, and appeals against decisions (referenced as tables B38–B43).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural data provide context on offices' processing activity and capacity and help interpret application/registration trends (e.g., how resources affect registrations issued and pendency). Specific definitions and measurement approaches are provided in the report's statistical tables and glossary.
